newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's blue chip stocks end week higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's blue chip stocks end week higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its weekly trading on Friday 2.8 percent higher, lifted by blue chip companies which gained up to 94 dirhams in the five-day trading, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 493.06 points against 479.48 points last Friday.

"The blue chip firms continue to drive the market higher for the fourth consecutive week...But foreign investors seem less excited, waiting for new flotations to return to the market," a Casablanca-based broker said.
Consumer credit firm Credor, floated on the bourse in December 1996, gained 94 dirhams in one week to close at 693 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Wafabank, one of the market's liquid stock, rose 63 dirhams to close at 663 dirhams.
Spanish Uniban bank, which is to merge with Wafabank, was traded at 123 dirhams, up five dirhams over the previous week.
Uniban expects its merger with Wafabank to be approved by main shareholders in February, the official said. Wafabank decided to buy 100 percent of Uniban at around $28 million.
Uniban showed a 27.2 million dirhams ($2.9 million) loss in 1995 due mainly to provisions for non-performing debt, a bank official said.

Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique, rose 25 dirhams to close at 178 dirhams. Morocco said it would soon sell its 34.57 percent stake in the bank. The tender closed on Friday. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the most competitive banks, rose six dirhams to close at 420 dirhams. BMCE plans to cut its interest rate by 0.25 percent on loans to small and medium enterprises starting from February 1.

ONA group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, closed at 626 dirhams, up 10 dirhams over the previous week. The conglomerate, which holds stakes in more than 100 firms, is the first market capitalisation with more than 10 billion dirhams.
It expects exceptional consolidated 1996 profit of 800 million dirhams ($87 million), a market analyst said.
Traded volume on the official market was 81.1 million dirhams from 63.6 million dirhams last Friday.
